thread.title: Bears On Track To End Nasdaq's Five-Day Win Streak | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Bears On Track To End Nasdaq's Five-Day Win Streak | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks were sharply lower in afternoon trade Thursday, with the Nasdaq composite on track to end a five-session win streak. Meanwhile, stock chart readers are finding qualified hope in the Nasdaq's chart.
X The Nasdaq skidded 1.7% Thursday afternoon, while the Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 fell 1.7% and 1.3%, respectively. Small caps outperformed with a smaller, 0.2% loss in the Russell 2000.
Volume was running higher on both major exchanges.
Stock chart readers see hope in the Nasdaq's three waves down since Oct. 1. The first wave down took the tech-leaning index down to 6922, the second to 6830 and the third to 6192. The indexes began rebounding after the Christmas Eve session.
Case For Bottom Arguable Many times a decline will bottom on either the third or fourth wave down. However, the current case is arguable for two reasons. First, neither the S&P 500 nor the Dow Jones has matched the Nasdaq's three lower lows. Second, the time frame for the current pattern is very short.
Still, the Christmas Eve closing low does not appear in danger. The Nasdaq remains about 5% to 6% above the low.
Bears Beat Down Apple Apple ( AAPL ) championed the bear cause Thursday. The stock violated its Christmas Eve low with an 8% dive. Unexpectedly weak sales guidance was behind the move. In mid-December, IBD noted Apple's lackluster performance in 2018. The widely held stock fell 7% in 2018.
Apple is about 38% off its early October high.
In the IBD 50 , a proxy for top stocks, only a handful of stocks were up in afternoon trade. Store Capital ( STOR ), a property REIT, rose 1.5%. Kirkland Lake Gold ( KL ) advanced 1.9%. Lululemon Athletica ( LULU ) popped 2%.
Blue chips in the 30-component Dow, were mostly down. Besides Apple, other Dow stocks hit hard included chipmaker Intel ( INTC ), off 3.5%, and Caterpillar ( CAT ), down 3%.
In the S&P 500, Bristol-Myers Squibb ( BMY ) gapped down about 14% in heavy volume. Bristol-Myers announced it would buy Celgene ( CELG ), a large-cap biotech. Celgene soared 24% on the news.
Celgene fell 39% in 2018. Bristol-Myers dropped 15%.
Economic Data The Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing gauge rolled in at 54.1 for December, which was below the entire range of estimates. Still, readings above 50 point to economic growth.
Some market watchers noted that Thursday's manufacturing drop was the biggest drop since October 2008, but that use of statistics is disingenuous. Here's what the pessimists are leaving out: In October 2008, the manufacturing gauge failed to grow for a third consecutive month. The 2008 reading was going deeper into contraction. The current reading continues to show growth, though slower than November's 59.3 reading.
ADP's private employment report for December came in at 271,000 jobs added, above the entire range of estimates and 55% higher than expected.
First-time jobless claims hit 231,000, about 6% worse than expected.
